title: The session-load docs say arm B leaves out the pane's --receipt run, so it understates the pane
goal: kb/_self/benchmarks.md and the session-load section of kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md say, in their arm B paragraphs, that the kbmon-pane mod's first refresh also runs kbmon.py --receipt (about as costly as --once) and arm B does not, so arm B's kbmon figures understate the mod's by about one --once-sized run in a 150 s window, and that arm B's kbmon reads an empty coord store and query log; no arm B paragraph calls a pane run the heavier refresh

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import re
for path in ('kb/_self/benchmarks.md', 'kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md'):
    text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    paras = [p for p in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', text) if 'arm B' in p or 'Arm B' in p]
    assert paras, ('no arm B paragraph', path)
    for p in paras:
        assert 'heavier refresh' not in p, ('an arm B paragraph still calls the pane run the heavier refresh', path)
    assert any('--receipt' in p for p in paras), ('no arm B paragraph says the mod also runs --receipt and arm B does not', path)
    assert any('empty' in p and ('coord' in p or 'query log' in p) for p in paras), ('no arm B paragraph says its kbmon reads an empty coord store and query log', path)
